cause: Plain mmdebstrap --unshare-helper chroot re-entry creates namespaces but does not restore the /dev and /proc mounts cleaned after bootstrap. /dev/null became a regular file.

producer_chain.behavior: Ubuntu optional bpftool search invokes find /usr/lib/linux-tools/ /usr/lib/linux-tools-* with stderr redirected to /dev/null. Absent optional directories are normal and must be discarded.

When generated triggers file does not yet exist, reads /dev/null as empty input then copies every input line to the new trigger file. A regular contaminated /dev/null propagates diagnostics into metadata.

repair: Bind host character devices null, zero, full, random, urandom, tty into the new private mount namespace before chroot; mount proc there. No broad host /dev exposure.
Before any build, assert character-device major/minor pairs, /dev/null discard/EOF, /dev/zero zeros and mounted proc.

Extract pristine authenticated Ubuntu source; rebuild complete versioned package set. Keep original patch and Ubuntu packaging semantics unchanged; never remove bad lines from existing package archives.
Require all30 packages control-file grammar checks plus clean official-resolute apt upgrade/remove-reinstall tests before package acceptance.

scope: No kernel/router/original rootfs changes. .1 artifacts preserved and rejected. Full PID1 credentials runtime acceptance remains separate.
